_schema: THE TOWN'S PEOPLE. One record per person; npc.js reads it and owns no coordinate, name or behaviour of its own. FIELDS — id: unique key. name: the E-prompt name (the dialogue window's nameplate comes from dialogue.json's speaker table, not from here). scene: a scene key or a LIST of them; a town villager lives in both the real-time explore bundle (townwalk) and the cinematic one (del-cine), which share the same world coordinates because del-cine ships the whole town's collision. position: RUNTIME [x, height, -y] — the town map authors [x, across-gorge, height], so a map pos [80.73, 16, 14] is [80.73, 14, -16] here. Every position below is a vertex of the town's own derived walk network (townmap/dellhollow.routes.json), so nobody stands off the path. facing: degrees; honoured by body.type 'model' and IGNORED by a billboard, which always turns to the camera. height: multiple of the engine's charH (MODEL_H, the [ / ] dial), so re-tuning the player re-tunes the town. body.type: 'billboard' (a chroma-keyed pose plate, today) or 'model' (a GLB, the day one exists — npc.js already loads it). body.src: the plate, page-relative. body.tint: multiplies the plate, which is how the chapter-2 expansion script dresses a REUSED villager sheet as somebody else ('reuse the poppy sheet, tint #d9b08a'); see bodyNote for who is wearing whose coat. idleBehavior: 'stand' | 'lean' (a few degrees into whatever they lean on) | 'wander' (a small errand on the walk network, WALKLOCK semantics: a step that leaves the network or hits a wall ends the errand). radius: talk reach in metres. dialogue: a node id in game/dialogue.json. shop: a shops.json id — marks a keeper, whose greeting node opens the counter via its own effect, so the player is greeted and THEN traded with.
_canon: Cast, placement and voice are from docs/chapter2-dellhollow-script.md, docs/chapter2-expansion-script.md and docs/VOICES.md. Odessa's post is the lockhead ('the senior lockkeeper's working post' — the town map says so); she and Maren live at the Keepers' Cottage. Hobb is nineteen days into the stopped queue; Pell keeps the wicks; Sorrel prices everything; Creel splices what the town hangs from; Nib administers the gulls. The eel-wife and the boatwright are canon ROLES the scripts name without naming (a woman selling eels, the boatwright's shed) and carry title nameplates rather than invented names. Nobody here carries a plot fact and nobody says the word 'afraid'.
_artNote: Only ten characters in public/assets/char-manifest.json ship a keyed pose plate, and five of these villagers (Hobb, Pell, Sorrel, Creel, Nib) are specified in the scripts as sprite-first, nameplate-only extras on REUSED, TINTED villager sheets. bodyNote records the loan for the art pipeline: replace src (and drop tint) the day the character is drawn, and nothing else changes.

npcs.name: Odessa
npcs.note: The Lockhead — her working post, overlooking Lock Five below. Canon station.

npcs.name: Maren
npcs.note: The lock apron between the moorage and Lock Five — the water end of the town, which is where she is when nobody is making her be anywhere else.

npcs.name: Captain Hobb
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed plate: finn, tinted ochre (nameplate-only extra, per script §b)
npcs.note: Leaning on his barge-pole by the slipway, where the stopped queue is rafted up.

npcs.name: Watchman Pell
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed plate: tally, tinted sage (nameplate-only extra, per script §b)
npcs.note: At the notice board, doing the noon wicks — the day shift, which is the grudge.

npcs.name: Sorrel
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed plate: poppy — the script names this sheet for Sorrel by name
npcs.note: The Harbour Deck at the market-stall end: her bread-window, relocated to the quay the town actually built.

npcs.name: Old Creel
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed plate: rowan, tinted pale (nameplate-only extra, per script §b)
npcs.note: The Weave's stilt-cluster deck — laundry lines, drying racks, rope bridges: everything that hangs.

npcs.name: Nib
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed plate: pip — the script asks for the smallest villager sheet available
npcs.note: The fish dock, where the gulls are — an eight-year-old's whole civil service.

npcs.name: Eel-wife
npcs.note: 'A woman selling eels shouted a price at them on principle' — Beat 2, verbatim. Title nameplate: the scripts never give her a name and neither do we.

npcs.name: Boatwright
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed plate: rowan, tinted tar-and-timber (42 m and a district away from Creel's loan of the same sheet)
npcs.note: At the pitch kettle below the boatwright's shed — tar smoke curling over the water, which is the smell of the boatyard and also his first line.

npcs.name: the cat
npcs.note: 'Mochi has located the eel-stall. The party's marching order has quietly changed.' — Beat 2. He is at the fish dock because of course he is.

npcs.name: chandler
npcs.note: Behind the counter of the Chandlery — lamp oil, rope, pitch, cantilevered out over the gorge.
